name: PlayStation Move Motion Controller
notes: 178-byte descriptor the device serves over USB, read over hidraw from a real Move (LKML, Pavel Machek, 2015-03-14, "Re: Fun with sony motion controllers: motion controller"): input 0x01 (48 bytes), outputs 0x02 (48) and 0x06 (8), features 0x03, 0x04, 0x05, 0x10, 0x11, 0xA0, 0xA1 and 0xE0. Its HID view is 24 buttons, three vendor bytes, four axes a real Move holds at 0x7F and 38 vendor bytes, so the input report is written whole from extendedReport where psmoveapi reads it (psmove.c PSMove_Data_Input_Common at 97d97e9, moveonpc wiki Input report at 033ab8e): Select and Start in byte 1, Triangle, Circle, Cross and Square in byte 2, PS, Move and T in byte 3 with Move and T again in byte 4 above the sequence number, the T trigger in bytes 5 and 6, battery in byte 12, and accelerometer then gyro in bytes 13 to 36, each twice for the two half-frames, as offset binary (psmove_decode_16bit). The T trigger is the left trigger, as RPCS3 reports it (ps_move_handler.cpp get_is_left_trigger at c82221f), and the Move button is Misc1. The raw motion values are the device's own axes in psmoveapi's order. The timestamp bytes 11 and 43 and the magnetometer stay zero. This is a ZCM1, PID 0x03D5.
